style_context: Crime prevention concepts including community safety, law enforcement, cybersecurity, home security, and youth leadership

images.description: A diverse group of neighbors gathered on a residential sidewalk on a sunny afternoon, talking with a community police officer in uniform. Well-maintained homes with trimmed landscaping and bright porch lights visible in the background. Adults and teenagers in casual clothes engaged in friendly conversation. Warm, welcoming neighborhood atmosphere.

Clean infographic showing four categories of crime arranged in a two-by-two grid. Top left: Property Crimes with icons of a house, car, and flame. Top right: Crimes Against People with icons of a shield and warning symbol. Bottom left: White Collar Crime with icons of a briefcase, document, and dollar sign. Bottom right: Environmental Crime with icons of a factory, tree, and water droplet. Each quadrant uses a distinct color and includes 3-4 example crime names in small text. Title at top reads Types of Crime.

A circular diagram showing seven groups that contribute to crime prevention. Seven labeled circles arranged in a ring: Citizens at top, then clockwise Schools, Community Groups, Private Security, Law Enforcement, Courts, and Corrections. Each circle has a simple icon inside (people, school building, handshake, shield, badge, gavel, building). Lines connect each circle to its neighbors and to a central circle labeled Crime Prevention. Clean white background with blue and teal color scheme.

A teenager's study desk viewed from slightly above. An open laptop showing a news website with text and charts visible on screen. A spiral notebook with handwritten notes next to the laptop. A few printed pages with bar charts showing crime statistics. A highlighter and pen resting on the notebook. Natural daylight from a nearby window. Clean, organized workspace feel.

A clean infographic with three large rectangular boxes arranged in a row. Left box has a person silhouette icon above the bold label Motivated Offender. Center box has a target bullseye icon above the bold label Suitable Target. Right box has an empty shield icon above the bold label Absence of Guardian. A large bold heading at the top reads The Crime Triangle. Below the three boxes, a single line of text reads Remove any one element to prevent the crime. Simple flat design, dark blue and white color scheme, no diagonal or angled text.

Split-frame comparison of the same residential street. LEFT side labeled Poor Design: overgrown bushes blocking windows, a burned-out streetlight, peeling paint on a fence, an alley with no lighting, and no people visible. Dull, gray tones. RIGHT side labeled Good Design: the same street with neatly trimmed low bushes, bright working streetlights, fresh paint, a front porch with chairs, and a neighbor walking a dog on the sidewalk. Warm, bright tones. Clear visual contrast between neglected and well-maintained environments.

A teenager in a clean Scout uniform holding a clipboard with a printed checklist, walking alongside an adult along the exterior of a single-family home. They are looking up at an exterior light fixture mounted near the garage. The home has a mix of good and improvable security features visible: a deadbolt on the front door, but bushes partially blocking a window. Daytime, clear weather.

A teenager standing at the front of a small meeting room, gesturing toward a simple poster on a whiteboard showing a basic home security diagram with labeled points. Four younger Scouts sitting in chairs facing the presenter, paying attention. The presenter looks confident and engaged. Bright indoor lighting, a Scout-appropriate meeting space.

Interior of a brightly lit retail store aisle. Visible security features annotated with labeled callout arrows: a convex security mirror mounted in the upper corner reflecting the aisle below, a dome security camera on the ceiling, an electronic article surveillance tag attached to a piece of clothing on a rack, and a store employee visible at the end of the aisle greeting a customer. Clean, well-organized store environment. Labels point to: Security Mirror, CCTV Camera, EAS Tag, Attentive Staff.

A teenager standing in a well-lit public area near a park pavilion, holding a smartphone to their ear with a calm but alert expression. Other people visible in the background going about normal activities. Good lighting from overhead park lights. The scene conveys that the teenager has moved to a safe, populated location before making a phone call.

A group of five teenagers working together on a community service project in a park. Two are painting a park bench with fresh paint, one is picking up litter with a grabber tool, and two are planting flowers along a pathway. They are wearing work gloves and casual work clothes. Smiling and talking to each other while working. Bright sunny day with green grass and trees in the background.

A school auditorium with rows of teenagers in clean Scout uniforms sitting attentively, all facing forward toward a stage. A speaker in business casual attire stands at a podium on the stage. A large banner behind the speaker reads Drug Free Communities. Bright overhead auditorium lighting. The scene is orderly and engaged, with the audience clearly paying attention to the presentation.

Clean infographic showing six online security best practices arranged in a two-column grid. Each practice has an icon and short label: 1. Strong Passwords icon of a lock with stars, 2. Two-Factor Authentication icon of a phone with a checkmark, 3. Software Updates icon of a refresh arrow on a shield, 4. Privacy Settings icon of an eye with a slash through it, 5. Verify Before Clicking icon of a magnifying glass over a link, 6. Report Suspicious Activity icon of a flag. Title at top reads Stay Safe Online. Blue and green color scheme on white background.

A teenager in a clean Scout uniform sitting in a chair across a desk from a police officer in a police station office. The teenager has a notebook open and is writing while listening. The officer is leaning forward slightly, engaged in conversation. A few items on the desk: a nameplate, a coffee mug, a framed certificate on the wall behind the officer. Professional but friendly atmosphere.

A four-panel infographic showing different crime prevention careers. Panel 1 labeled Forensic Scientist: a person in a lab coat examining evidence under a microscope in a laboratory. Panel 2 labeled Cybersecurity Analyst: a person at a desk with multiple computer monitors showing code and network diagrams. Panel 3 labeled Community Officer: a police officer in uniform talking with residents at a neighborhood event. Panel 4 labeled Urban Planner: a person reviewing architectural blueprints and neighborhood maps at a desk. Each panel is a clean illustrated style with career title below. Title at top reads Careers in Crime Prevention.
